pensamiento:
I'm checking the first user story (QUS-001) against the quality criteria: it names a developer role and an action, so it passes. For QUS-002, the story lists several browsers but still asks for one thing, browser compatibility, so I'm treating it as passing too, though it's borderline.

I'm going through the rest of the user stories against the criteria. QUS-006 fails because "function correctly" and "as many people as possible" aren't measurable, so that's a major problem. The other stories look fine, and INV-003 is ambiguous since "correctly" is never defined.

I'm weighing INV-003 as a clear fail, since it's unclear which functions are in scope and what "correctly" would be tested against. INV-004 looks large because it spans five browser versions across the whole app, so it needs an estimate and a look at references. INV-005 has no acceptance criteria, which blocks it. The DOR checks on dependencies, business rules and non-functional requirements don't seem to apply here, though the compatibility requirement is borderline for the last one.

I'm working through the remaining items: DOR-001 through DOR-003 look like they don't apply here, since there are no evident external dependencies, business-rule limits, or high-volume concerns. The real defects are QUS-006, INV-003, and INV-005, with INV-004 possibly too large. Next I need to check references and the estimation scale.

pensamiento:
I'm deciding to send this back, since defects QUS-006, INV-003, and INV-005 are still open. The scope looks very large, covering the whole app across five browsers, so a reliable estimate is hard. The rule says to register a 1 when the story doesn't describe an estimable scope, and the unclear set of functions makes me wonder whether that applies here. I'm weighing a 5-8 range, leaning toward an 8.

I'm weighing whether the defect list should include INV-004, since the scope is possibly large but its estimate can't really be determined. I'll leave it out and mention it as a note on INV-003 in the recommendations. The refined story will keep the same listed functions and browsers without adding any scope.

I'm leaving the acceptance criteria empty, since this one is being sent back and the schema only requires them when accepting. I'll still write a refined story that keeps the same functions and browsers without adding scope, and cap each recommendation at 600 characters.

He revisado EV-19 y dejé la recomendación en borrador como **devolver**, pendiente de aprobación humana.

Tiene tres defectos, todos de criterios de calidad o de aceptación: QUS-006 (No ambigua), INV-003 (Estimable) e INV-005 (Verificable, bloqueante). recomendaciones.texto: Reemplazar 'funcione correctamente' y 'tantas personas como sea posible' por medidas observables: qué funciones o pantallas deben funcionar, y qué significa 'correctamente' (por ejemplo, flujos concretos completados sin errores de script ni de diseño).

Definir el alcance para poder estimar: qué funcionalidades o pantallas de la aplicación entran en la compatibilidad, y si las cinco versiones de navegador (IE 6 y 7, Firefox 1.5 y 2, Safari 2) aplican a todas. Sin esto el equipo tendría que preguntar el alcance antes de estimar.

Agregar criterios de aceptación verificables, uno por navegador y versión, con un resultado observable. Ejemplo de formato: 'Con IE 6, al completar [flujo acordado], la operación termina y se muestra [resultado esperado]'. Los flujos deben definirlos el analista.

revision.historia_refinada: Como developer, quiero que la aplicación funcione correctamente en Internet Explorer 6 y 7, Firefox 1.5 y 2, y Safari 2, para que el mayor número posible de personas pueda usar la aplicación completa.
